properties.name: Itai Cohen Group
properties.description:
**Itai Cohen** — Cornell University, Ithaca, NY (US)

Builds microscopic robots -- roughly 5 microns thick, 40-70 microns long, the size of a paramecium -- from a simple circuit with silicon photovoltaics as torso and brain, and electrochemical actuators as legs. Shining laser light on the photovoltaics walks the robots. Demonstrated up to ~1 million robots fabricated per silicon wafer.

**Why it's on this map:** Builds genuinely autonomous, sub-100-micron robots with onboard photovoltaic power and onboard actuation -- about as close a match as exists anywhere to a real whole-system microrobot, and a strong technical reference point.

[[https://cohengroup.lassp.cornell.edu/|Group website]]

Category: Micro-Robotics Lab · Smallest demonstrated: 5 µm

properties.name: Paul McEuen Group
properties.description:
**Paul McEuen** — Cornell University, Ithaca, NY (US)

Room 109
https://physics.cornell.edu/paul-mceuen



The science and technology of nanostructures, particularly carbon-based systems such as nanotubes and graphene; novel fabrication techniques at the nanometer scale; micro- and nanoscale machines and active matter; assembly and measurement of chemical and biological nanostructures
Research Focus

Our research focuses on the fabrication and study of nanostructures. We use these structures to span the gap between the macroscopic and molecular worlds, exploring electronics, optics, mechanics, chemistry and biology at the nanoscale. Current research ranges from the use of carbon nanotubes for optoelectronics and mechanics to the use of graphene and other 2D materials for atomic-scale origami, active materials, and micro and nanomachines.

**Why it's on this map:** Works on nanostructure fabrication and micro/nanoscale active matter and machines -- closely related in technique to sub-millimeter robotics, part of a small cluster of collaborating groups at the same university.

[[https://physics.cornell.edu/paul-mceuen|Group website]]

Category: Micro-Robotics Lab · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Oliver G. Schmidt's Lab
properties.description:
**Oliver G. Schmidt** — TU Chemnitz, Chemnitz (DE)

Research areas: microrobotics and micromotors; biomedical applications; flexible and shapeable electronics; energy storage at the micro/nanoscale; magnetoelectronics; micro- and nanoelectronics; microfluidics; plasmonics.

**Latest research/products of interest:** SMARTLET microrobot, MICMOS microrobot

**Why it's on this map:** One of a small number of groups worldwide that build genuinely whole, autonomous sub-millimeter robotic systems -- a top-tier reference point, and unusually close geographically.

[[https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/etit/nano/OliverGSchmidt.php|Group website]]

Category: Micro-Robotics Lab · Smallest demonstrated: 100 µm

properties.name: Intelligent Microrobotics Laboratory (IML)
properties.description:
**Wei Wang** — Westlake University, Hangzhou (CN)

Designs and fabricates CMOS-circuit-compatible intelligent microrobotics: CMOS circuit design for microrobotics, structure design for micro machines, and nanofabrication for building them. Research interests include micro-robotics, origami, MEMS, and cilia-based actuation.

**Why it's on this map:** Works on microrobotics designed to be compatible with standard CMOS circuit fabrication -- an unusually close match for anyone pursuing a chip-fabrication-based approach to building small autonomous robots.

[[https://wangwei.lab.westlake.edu.cn/|Group website]]

Category: Micro-Robotics Lab · Smallest demonstrated: unknown
